title: Tables
author: ERgzLEN9pchn62XKb
chapter_outcomes: Understand the structure of these qualifications as modular qualifications where the International Advanced Subsidiary can be claimed on completion of the IAS units, and the International Advanced Level can be claimed on completion of all units (IAS and IA2 units)

Understand that the content covers major topics in biology, including biological molecules, diet, transport, health, cells, development, biodiversity, conservation, energy, the environment, microbiology, immunity, respiration, the internal environment, coordination and gene technology

Understand that assessment consists of three written papers at IAS level that are externally assessed, and the International A level consists of three further written papers that are externally assessed
Understand that students will develop their knowledge and understanding of biology by applying the concepts in this specification to a range of different problems, set in a variety of contexts

Understand that students will need to apply mathematical skills to problems, with the qualification including questions that target mathematics at Level 2 or above, with overall a minimum of 10 percent of the marks across the papers awarded for mathematics at Level 2 or above

Understand that students will also develop their practical skills, with this specification including 18 core practical activities, which is the minimum number of practical activities that students will carry out

Know the assessment objectives: AO1 (Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of science), AO2a (Application of knowledge and understanding of science in familiar and unfamiliar contexts), AO2b (Analysis and evaluation of scientific information to make judgments and reach conclusions), AO3 (Experimental skills in science, including analysis and evaluation of data and methods)

Understand the qualification structure: International Advanced Subsidiary consists of three externally examined units (Units 1, 2, and 3), and International Advanced Level consists of six externally examined units (Units 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6)

Know that Unit 1: Molecules, Diet, Transport and Health is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 30 minutes, worth 80 marks, representing 40% of the total IAS and 20% of the total IAL

Know that Unit 2: Cells, Development, Biodiversity and Conservation is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 30 minutes, worth 80 marks, representing 40% of the total IAS and 20% of the total IAL
Know that Unit 3: Practical Skills in Biology I is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 20 minutes, worth 50 marks, representing 20% of the total IAS and 10% of the total IAL

Know that Unit 4: Energy, Environment, Microbiology and Immunity is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 45 minutes, worth 90 marks, representing 40% of the total IA2 and 20% of the total IAL

Know that Unit 5: Respiration, Internal Environment, Coordination and Gene Technology is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 45 minutes, worth 90 marks, representing 40% of the total IA2 and 20% of the total IAL, with pre-released reading (scientific article) provided for this assessment

Know that Unit 6: Practical Skills in Biology II is externally assessed through written examination of 1 hour and 20 minutes, worth 50 marks, representing 20% of the total IA2 and 10% of the total IAL
Understand that papers may include multiple-choice, short-open, open-response, calculations and extended-writing questions
Understand that candidates will be expected to apply their knowledge and understanding to familiar and unfamiliar contexts
Understand that papers 4 and 5 may contain synoptic questions which require knowledge and understanding from units 1 and 2
Know that calculators may be used in the examination
Understand the grading system: International Advanced Subsidiary is graded on a five-grade scale from A to E, and International Advanced Level is graded on a six-point scale from A* to E

Know that to be awarded an A*, candidates will need to achieve an A for the International Advanced Level qualification (at least 480 uniform marks) and at least 90 percent of the total uniform marks available across the IA2 units combined (at least 270 uniform marks)

Understand the transferable skills framework based on the National Research Council's framework, including cognitive skills (cognitive processes and strategies, creativity), intrapersonal skills (intellectual openness, work ethic/conscientiousness, positive core self-evaluation), and interpersonal skills (teamwork and collaboration, leadership)
